newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cinemas call off month-long strike.
newsitem.headline: Indian cinemas call off month-long strike.

text.p: Cinema owners in India's film capital of Bombay on Tuesday called off a month long strike to protest against a steep hike in entertainment tax, a top state official told Reuters.
"The theatre-owners have unilaterally called off their strike," Maharashtra Culture Minister Pramod Navalkar told Reuters. "They notified us this afternoon."
The cinema owners had protested that the hike proposed by the Shiv Sena government in Maharashtra state would double ticket prices and drive away filmgoers.

"Theatres will open on Friday," said Balkrishna Shroff, one of Bombay's leading film distributors. "We are releasing three new films. The public has been starved, so to speak, and we are expecting a positive impact."
The strike began on January 1, when the new rate of tax was scheduled to go into effect. About 1,300 theatres across the state participated in the strike, including 106 Bombay cinemas.
The cinemas will charge patrons at the old rates when they reopen, Shroff said. "We have left everything in the hands of the government," he added.
Navalkar said the government had been unable to negotiate with the cinema owners because of election rules that forbid it to make announcements of any concessions ahead of polls.
A series of elections to self-government bodies at the city and village levels in Maharashtra, where Bombay is located, are scheduled to run through February, an election official said.
A poll code of conduct that takes effect during this period prevented the government from announcing any tax cuts, he said.
"I am pleased that the cinema owners have called off their strike," Navalkar said. "The state government was losing about two million rupees in tax every day."
He estimated losses to the film industry at about four million rupees ($112,000) for each day of the strike, he added.
But industry officials had earlier placed the figure at 7.5 million rupees.
The strike had paralysed the exhibition, marketing and distribution sectors of the film industry, though actors and directors continued to shoot movies in Bombay film studios.
Many films slated for release during the first two weeks of January were also delayed, industry officials said.
